To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the fate of the pesticides in the soil was strongly dependent on the soil concentration and that the fate of both pesticides was strongly dependent on their soil concentration.
the fate of atrazines and PCP in soils is influenced by the concentration of these pesticides, the type of plant species, the presence of other pesticides and the environmental conditions.
The fate of pesticides in soil is influenced by many factors.

the development and application of a novel approach, the “microbial community fingerprinting” to assess the impact of environmental factors on soil microbial communities.
the fate and behavior of the herbicide atrazine and the fungicide pentachlorophenate in soil and in the plant root zone.

the results of the laboratory experiments with the two pesticides were in good agreement with those from the outdoor experiments.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
atrazine and PCP are not very mobile in soil and are not readily available to the plants.
the laboratory system was a useful tool for studying the fate of pesticides in soil, but that the results must not be extrapolated to field conditions without further studies.

the laboratory data are useful to get an overview of the general behavior of a compound, but they cannot replace field studies, especially for long‐term studies and for compounds with a high potential for bioaccumulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the soil and the plant can act as a sink for the pesticides and their metabolites and thus reduce their mobility and availability for further degradation and uptake.

the soil is an important reservoir for the accumulation and persistence of atrazine and pentachloro‐phenol in the soil-plant system and that the soil is a major source for the formation of 14C in the atmosphere.

, although the majority of studies have focused on the effects of pesticides on the soil ecosystem, the effects of pesticides and their metabolites on the soil ecosystem are not limited to the soil ecosystem.
